# AGENTS.md

## What this repo is

GR-HEEP is a **vendorization wrapper around X-HEEP**: the SoC RTL comes from the vendored copy in `hw/vendor/x-heep/` (pinned by `hw/vendor/x-heep.vendor.hjson`). The root Makefile delegates any target it doesn't define to X-HEEP's Makefile via `hw/vendor/x-heep/external.mk` — that `include` must stay **last** in the root Makefile (its `%:` catch-all relies on it). X-HEEP's own `hw/vendor/x-heep/AGENTS.md` also applies.

## Generated files — never edit directly

`make mcu-gen` (X-HEEP's Mako generator) regenerates these from `.tpl` templates; edit the `.tpl` instead:

- `hw/gr-heep/gr_heep.sv`, `gr_heep_pad_ring.sv`, `gr_heep_peripherals.sv`, `gr_heep_pkg.sv` (from `hw/gr-heep/*.tpl`; `gr_heep_bus.sv` and `gr_heep_xbar.sv` are static)
- `tb/tb_util.svh` (from `tb/tb_util.svh.tpl`)
- `sw/external/lib/runtime/gr_heep.h` (from `.tpl`)

Generated files are gitignored — they are not committed. `mcu-gen` also runs `make verible` (format + lint) on `hw/gr-heep/*.sv`; CI's lint job runs `mcu-gen` and fails if any tracked file differs, so keep static RTL verible-clean.

## Configuration

- `config/mcu-gen-config.py` — the central SoC config: bus type, CPU (cv32e40px), RAM banks, linker sections, base/user peripheral domains, interrupt map, and the GR-HEEP extension (`gr_heep_config()` for external slaves/peripherals). Almost every hardware change starts here.
- `config/gr-heep_pad_cfg.py` — pad ring configuration.
- After changing any config or `.tpl`: re-run `make mcu-gen` (or `make test`, which runs it first).

## Environment

- Python tooling (fusesoc, etc.): the Makefile uses `./.venv/bin/` unless a conda env is active (`CONDA_DEFAULT_ENV`). Setup: `make venv` (X-HEEP's) or `make conda` + `conda activate x-heep`.
- `RISCV_XHEEP` must point to the RISC-V toolchain (without `/bin`); `COMPILER_PREFIX` is auto-detected from it (`riscv32-corev-` default, `riscv32-unknown-` alternative).
- Toolchain container: `ghcr.io/x-heep/x-heep/x-heep-toolchain` (CI picks the tag matching the vendored X-HEEP version).

## Commands

```bash
make mcu-gen                                  # generate RTL+SW headers for TARGET (default asic)
make app PROJECT=hello_world                  # build firmware -> sw/build/main.hex
make verilator-build                          # build Verilator model (after RTL changes)
make verilator-run-app                        # build app + simulate it
make test                                     # mcu-gen + compile & simulate all apps (verilator)
make test TEST_FLAGS=--compile-only           # fast: compile only
make vivado-fpga FPGA_BOARD=pynq-z2           # FPGA bitstream (also nexys-a7-100t, genesys2, aup-zu3, zcu102, zcu104)
make verible                                  # format+lint SystemVerilog
make format-python                            # black on config/ and test/ only
```

- `make test` runs `test/gr_heep_test_apps.py`: every app in `hw/vendor/x-heep/sw/applications` (whitelisted there) plus **every** app in `sw/applications` is compiled for the `on_chip` linker and simulated. Adding an app under `sw/applications` adds it to CI. The script builds the Verilator model itself (`make verilator-build`), so no pre-built model is needed.
- `make TARGET=<board>` selects FPGA vs ASIC flow; unsupported values error out.
- FuseSoC core is `gr-heep.core` (`x-heep:systems:gr-heep`); sim build lands in `build/x-heep_systems_gr-heep_*/sim-verilator` (or `sim-modelsim`).

## CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

Gate order (via job needs): `lint` + `check-vendor` + `black-formatter` → `simulate-apps`.

- **lint**: `make mcu-gen`, then git-diff — fails if generation or verible formatting changes any tracked file.
- **check-vendor**: re-runs `util/vendor.py` on every `hw/vendor/*.vendor.hjson` and fails on diffs.
- **black-formatter**: `black --check` on `config` and `test`, pinned `~= 24.8.0`.
- **simulate-apps**: `make mcu-gen && python3 test/gr_heep_test_apps.py`.

## Vendored X-HEEP

- Do **not** hand-edit files under `hw/vendor/x-heep/` for a fix you intend to keep: CI re-vendors and rejects in-place edits. For quick local debugging it's fine, but the change must go upstream or into a patch (`hw/vendor/patches/x-heep/`, referenced by `patch_dir` in the vendor hjson).
- Never edit `hw/vendor/x-heep.lock.hjson` (generated by `util/vendor.py`).
- Upstream updates are automated: the nightly `xheep-canary` workflow bumps the rev, runs CI, and pushes to `main` only if it passes; failures open an issue. Don't bump the rev manually.
